title: MCP server documentation
intro: GlassFolio lets AI clients such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Antigravity use its tools on your own data. This page explains how it works, how to connect a client, and what the tools do.

howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.body: Your vault is encrypted in your browser, and only your open GlassFolio tab holds the key: no program can read it from outside. The MCP server is therefore a bridge that runs on your own computer. Your AI client sends it a tool call, the bridge passes the call to your tab, the tab runs the tool on your data and sends the result back. Nothing goes through GlassFolio’s servers, and the bridge stores nothing.

needs.title: What you need
needs.a: Node.js 22 and a copy of the repository: the bridge is mcp-server/index.mjs and has no dependency.
needs.b: GlassFolio open in a browser tab, signed in, with your vault unlocked.
needs.c: “Allow AI clients” turned on in Settings, AI & MCP.
needs.d: An AI client that supports MCP over stdio or Streamable HTTP.
needs.checkLabel: Check that the bridge starts and lists its tools

local.title: GlassFolio running on your machine (Docker or npm run dev)
local.body: The server of the app already contains the bridge, at its /mcp address: there is nothing else to start. Settings, AI & MCP shows the address and the token to give to your client.

online.title: GlassFolio online (app.glassfolio.dev)
online.body: Start the bridge on your computer. Your tab then connects to it at 127.0.0.1, the way it does for a local Ollama model, so nothing leaves your machine. Paste its token in Settings, AI & MCP. Some browsers ask for your permission before a web page reaches a local address, and some may block it: if yours does, use the local mode.
online.label: Start the bridge and print its token

connect.title: Connect your AI client
connect.body: Give your client the address of the bridge and its token (header X-GlassFolio-Token), or let it start the command itself. Settings, AI & MCP prepares these snippets with your own values.
connect.stdio: Clients that start a command (Claude Desktop and others)
connect.note: Replace the path with the folder of your copy of the repository. Other clients, such as Cursor or Antigravity, take the same information in their own MCP settings: the address and the token, or the command.

approvals.title: Changes need your approval
approvals.body: A tool that changes your data, such as recording a transaction or creating a goal, does not run when the client asks. GlassFolio shows a card in your open tab, and the change is made only if you approve it there. If you do not answer within about a minute and a half, nothing is changed. In read-only mode, these tools are blocked.

privacy.title: What leaves your computer
privacy.body: The results of the tools go to your AI client, and from there to the model it uses, as when you paste figures into a chat. API keys, recovery keys and authenticator seeds are removed before a result leaves GlassFolio. If nothing must leave your machine, connect a client that runs a local model.

limits.title: Limits
limits.a: The tab has to stay open and unlocked. If you lock the vault or close the tab, the client is told to ask you to open GlassFolio again.
limits.b: One tab serves the clients at a time: opening a second tab takes over.
limits.c: The bridge listens on your own computer only and accepts only the token that you share.

clients.title: Compatible clients
clients.body: Any client that supports MCP over stdio or Streamable HTTP can use it. {{tested}}

tools.title: Tools
tools.intro: The {{count}} tools that the bridge offers, as your client sees them (the descriptions are in English). The ones marked “Needs your approval” change your data and wait for it.

more.title: Going further
more.body: The assistant inside the app uses the same tools. To run the whole app on your own machine, read the self-hosting guide.
